# Discovery fixtures

SQLite tag-list and `3.54.0` release HTML are responses captured on 2026-10-13 from https://sqlite.org/src/taglist and https://sqlite.org/releaselog/3_54_0.html. Only trailing whitespace and trailing blank lines are normalized for repository checks. They exercise the actual Fossil presentation, including historical tags outside the discovery baseline. They are publication metadata, not vendored upstream sources.


Captured HTML is stored as `.html.txt` and read only as text/bytes by the offline readers. Its embedded upstream JavaScript is inert fixture data, not executable project code. The extension change preserves all captured bytes; tests do not load these files in a browser.

The SQLite-Vector JSON files are captured metadata from 2026-10-19: release [375995593](https://api.github.com/repos/sqliteai/sqlite-vector/releases/375995593), tag [1.1.0](https://api.github.com/repos/sqliteai/sqlite-vector/git/ref/tags/1.1.0), and commit [235a7c51b18858e1fea9fb2895e115e4cbbd9f7d](https://api.github.com/repos/sqliteai/sqlite-vector/git/commits/235a7c51b18858e1fea9fb2895e115e4cbbd9f7d). The release fixture projects only ID/URLs/tag/classification/publication time; tag and commit records retain their returned metadata. JSON is pretty-printed and final newlines normalized. No source archive or qualification result is captured. These dated bytes are fixed test inputs, not a promise that mutable upstream metadata never changes. Synthetic prereleases, annotated tags, histories, candidates and failures are labelled in test names or construction comments; none claims an observed upstream alpha.
